free_tier.stated: No LFS storage quota is published and none is enforced in the docs. Microsoft states plainly: 'Azure DevOps Services fully supports Git LFS and offers it for free.' The free tier is 5 Basic users with unlimited private Git repos; only Azure Artifacts carries a numeric cap (2 GiB free). Repo size guidance is 250 GB (soft), 'recommend keeping below 10 GB for optimal performance'.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: Unmetered. No bandwidth line item exists anywhere on the Azure DevOps pricing page. The paid units are users, parallel jobs and Artifacts GiB only.

tooling: git-lfs 3.x (gitlfs/git-lfs). Works over HTTPS; SSH is NOT supported for repos with LFS-tracked files. PAT auth. Also reachable via the Azure DevOps REST API for repo/ref management.
chaining: 5 free Basic users per org, and up to 5 orgs per account (Microsoft Q&A, moderator answer) -> 25 orgs' worth of free LFS if each is a separate MSA. Orgs are unlimited in repo count, so total LFS is bounded only by the 250 GB-per-repo soft guidance. 250 GB x N repos. Unlike GitLab/GitHub, LFS bytes are not on the meter at all.
limits_note: LFS objects do NOT count toward the 5 GB push limit: 'Git LFS doesn't count towards the 5-GB repository limit. The 5-GB limit applies only to files in the actual repository, not to blobs stored with LFS.' Every push request is still capped at 5 GB and there is a one-hour upload limit per the docs ('Large uploads can be constrained by available free space, current workload, and the one-hour upload limit'). Non-LFS files cap at 100 MB. No per-LFS-file cap is documented.

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: The 250 GB repo figure is guidance, not a wall, but the docs warn the internal pack-file limit can trigger 'The Git pack file limit has been reached' and temporarily block writes on very large repos. Over-quota behaviour is undefined because there is no quota.
confidence_note: Unverified: carried from historical research records without live verification. A first-party page read confirms documentation.
